name: MathlibAnnex.BilipschitzOrientation.fderiv_lower_bound
title: A positive lower metric bound passes to the derivative

content.display_title: A positive lower metric bound passes to the derivative
content.one_sentence_role: Preserves the same lower constant in the difference-quotient limit.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and let $E=\mathbb R^n$ have the sup norm $\|\cdot\|_\infty$. Let $S,T\subseteq E$ be open, and let $f,g:E\to E$ be globally Lipschitz maps whose restrictions $f|_S:S\to T$ and $g|_T:T\to S$ are mutually inverse. Fix a number $\ell>0$ such that
$$\ell\|x-x'\|_\infty\le\|f(x)-f(x')\|_\infty\qquad(x,x'\in E).$$

Suppose $f$ is differentiable at a point $x\in E$. Let $Df(x):E\to E$ denote its Fréchet derivative there. Then
$$\ell\|v\|_\infty\le\|Df(x)v\|_\infty\qquad(v\in E).$$
content.assumptions:
The map $f$ is differentiable at this particular $x$; the point $x$ need not lie in $S$. The sets $S,T\subseteq E$ are open. The inverse and image conditions are
$$\begin{aligned}
f(S)&\subseteq T,&g(T)&\subseteq S,\\
g(f(x))&=x\quad(x\in S),&f(g(y))&=y\quad(y\in T).
\end{aligned}$$
The global bounds use specified constants $C_f,C_g\ge0$ and $\ell>0$:
$$\ell\|x-x'\|_\infty\le\|f(x)-f(x')\|_\infty\le C_f\|x-x'\|_\infty\qquad(x,x'\in E),$$
$$\|g(y)-g(y')\|_\infty\le C_g\|y-y'\|_\infty\qquad(y,y'\in E).$$
The estimates hold on all of $E$, not just on $S$ or $T$. The inverse identities are required only on $S$ and $T$.
content.conclusion:
The derivative has the same positive lower constant $\ell$ as the original map. In particular,
$$Df(x)v=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\ell\|v\|_\infty\le0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad v=0.$$
Thus $Df(x)$ is injective. The estimate also includes the direction $v=0$.
content.proof_summary: Apply the lower bound to $x+tv$ and $x$, divide by $|t|$, and pass to the derivative as $t\to0$.

proof_steps.text:
**Write the difference-quotient estimate.** Fix $v\in E$. For every real $t\ne0$,
$$\begin{aligned}
\ell |t|\|v\|_\infty&\le\|f(x+tv)-f(x)\|_\infty,\\
\ell\|v\|_\infty&\le\left\|\frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t}\right\|_\infty.
\end{aligned}$$
The first line is the global lower bound at these two points. The second follows from $|t|>0$ and homogeneity of the norm; it does not require $v\ne0$.

**Take the limit.** Differentiability at $x$ gives
$$\frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t}\longrightarrow Df(x)v\qquad(t\to0,\ t\ne0).$$
Consequently,
$$\ell\|v\|_\infty\le\lim_{t\to0,\ t\ne0}\left\|\frac{f(x+tv)-f(x)}{t}\right\|_\infty=\|Df(x)v\|_\infty.$$
This is precisely [the difference-quotient lemma](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Basic.lean#L99-L123) with linear map $Df(x)$, lower constant $\ell$, the displayed global estimate, and differentiability at $x$. No derivative at any other point is needed.

content.lean_realization_notes: Applying the same estimate to $u-v$ proves that $Df(x)u=Df(x)v$ forces $u=v$, as in [the derivative-injectivity corollary](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Basic.lean#L143-L148). Since $Df(x)$ is a linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space $E$, [the determinant corollary](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Basic.lean#L150-L157) gives $\det Df(x)\ne0$. Similarly, the original lower bound gives global injectivity of $f$ by applying it when $f(x)=f(x')$.
